title: Compaction follows compression.threshold again: no default 256K token cap
before: At parent 5912ed81ed945a784f67ca13c1096e2c122cd307, the canonical compression configuration set compression.threshold_tokens to 256000 and the schema version to 46. When the raw compression section omitted the key, agent construction fell back to that default and passed it as the compressor's absolute threshold cap. The compressor then used the lower of the ratio-derived trigger and the cap, so a 1M-token window with the default 0.50 ratio compacted at 256K rather than 500K; an explicit null was already an opt-out. The example configuration was version 46 and materialized threshold_tokens: 256000, and the shared seeding path copied that template into new configurations, turning the temporary default into a persisted literal that looked like a user choice. Existing gateway-cache and TUI hot-reload consumers also resolved an absent key through DEFAULT_CONFIG, so they treated absence as the 256K cap.
after: At 98278833e29b167fe930e276eed7cb16bee68673, compression.threshold_tokens is None in DEFAULT_CONFIG and the schema/template move to version 47. An absent key now constructs a compressor with no absolute cap, so the ratio- and model-derived trigger governs across context-window sizes; a positive user-supplied cap remains supported, is applied as the lower-of ratio-versus-absolute rule, and survives model switches. The new v47 migration removes threshold_tokens only when a versioned pre-v47 configuration contains exactly the stale 256000 default; other explicit caps and explicit null remain untouched. Because the gateway cache signature and TUI live-sync code already read the canonical default, their behavior follows the new policy: absent and explicit null are ratio-only, while an explicit positive cap remains a distinct cached/live configuration. Documentation and regression expectations now describe the absolute cap as opt-in.
diff: The commit changes 10 files with 73 insertions and 66 deletions. The production policy change is the DEFAULT_CONFIG flip from 256000 to None plus config schema v46 to v47; the example template becomes a commented optional cap and v47. A new v46-to-v47 migration uses the existing stale-default rewrite mechanism to delete only the exact old literal. The compressor algorithm, gateway cache extraction, and TUI live-sync implementation are not structurally changed because they already derive their fallback from DEFAULT_CONFIG; their tests are updated to assert the new default while preserving explicit-cap behavior. Three documentation pages are updated from a universal 256K cap to an optional absolute cost ceiling.

before: At parent commit 6cfa25c967e348104609ee17ab020635c23f6ca0, ordinary deferred tools were hidden from the initial declaration list and exposed through the existing on-demand discovery path; GeminiClient.startChat warmed the registry, handled resume-history reveals, and then resolved the deferred-tool reminder without any context-window budget decision.     window). At session start, when the combined estimated schema footprint

    the budget, all are revealed upfront so the declaration list stays

    everything stays deferred. Set 0 to always defer. Mirrors Claude Code's

    Emit debugLogger diagnostics in preloadDeferredToolsWithinBudget covering

    preloaded). Lets an operator diagnosing session-startup cost tell from debug
    logs whether the deferred set fit the budget or was left behind ToolSearch,

title: perf(core): chat history O(n^2) re-serialization on every turn causes jank on long sessions
before: The pinned commit's parent was af687798afe3b83fd8bf46e91d659c88347427ba. In the parent implementation, the interactive tool coordinator appended combined cancellation function responses to the durable chat history even when all model-initiated tools in the turn were cancelled. The interactive and legacy execution paths could also finish after a tool continuation that produced no visible response. For invalid-stream retries, GeminiChat appended retry nudges to the system instruction rather than to the end of the current request contents. The edit self-correction path did not reject a blank search string before invoking the correction helper, and no-match feedback was less specific.
after: The interactive coordinator records a history-length checkpoint before sending a prepared query and truncates the current history back to that checkpoint when all model-initiated tools are cancelled, without appending cancellation responses or issuing another model request. Interactive continuations now detect empty post-tool output and submit a recovery nudge with a per-user-query budget of two automatic attempts. The legacy execution loop performs the corresponding post-tool empty-response recovery once per armed tool-response cycle. GeminiChat now keeps systemInstruction stable and applies invalid-stream retry nudges to request contents, preserving role alternation and reapplying the nudge after hook content replacement. The edit invocation rejects missing or whitespace-only old_string before LLM correction and returns more actionable exact-match guidance. The commit also adds outgoing empty-part normalization and a wording-only attribution cleanup.
diff: Commit 812f7a2bcf20b6e80e2e50c3c8fa8e26567bc1e8 changes nine files: interactive stream coordination and tests, legacy agent/session behavior and tests, GeminiChat retry/content handling and tests, and Edit-tool validation and tests. The semantic changes are bounded cancellation-history rollback, bounded recovery after silent tool continuations, end-of-context retry nudging, payload-part normalization, and early edit-input rejection. The available evidence contains regression tests for the primary rollback, recovery, retry-placement, and edit-guard paths, but no performance benchmark proving the reported O(n^2) symptom or a dedicated test for the new empty-part sanitizer.

title: [Linux Desktop] local stdio MCP launch inherits unrelated app-server file descriptors into MCP servers and their children
before: The local Unix stdio launcher constructed a child command with piped stdin/stdout/stderr and a new process group, but did not set a descriptor-inheritance policy. The shared command builder therefore retained its default DescriptorPolicy::Inherit, allowing inheritable, unrelated descriptors held by the orchestrator to reach the local MCP server and any descendants it launched. The local runtime path selected LocalStdioServerLauncher for local stdio MCP configurations and passed that command through RmcpClient to the launcher.
after: The local Unix stdio launcher sets DescriptorPolicy::StdioOnly on every locally constructed MCP command. The existing Unix spawn backend then closes inheritable descriptors other than the explicit transport stdio before exec, while retaining the internal exec-error reporting path; the macOS native backend uses its close-on-exec-default path. The server and descendants therefore inherit only the explicitly wired stdio transport, while the existing process group, arguments, environment, working directory, MCP protocol exchange, and launch-error behavior remain intact. The change is guarded by cfg(unix); Windows behavior is intentionally unchanged and remains a deferred handle-allowlist concern.
diff: Commit afe4249cfe, parent b4b30dd5eb9994ddc51f915ecd74e9a8c1d93248, modifies codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/stdio_server_launcher.rs by adding Unix DescriptorPolicy support and applying command.descriptor_policy(DescriptorPolicy::StdioOnly) inside the local command builder. It adds codex-rs/rmcp-client/tests/stdio_descriptor_boundary.rs, a Unix-only integration test that creates inheritable pipe, socket, and file descriptors, verifies an unfiltered control launch sees them, then exercises absolute, relative, and shell-fallback local launches and asserts that neither the MCP server nor its descendant sees them. The test also checks MCP communication, arguments, environment, working directory, stderr, parent descriptor ownership after shutdown, and direct exec-failure reporting. No shared descriptor backend, remote executor path, or Windows implementation is changed.

title: Parallel tool execution drops tool_result for calls not yet reached when abort fires
before: At the parent ref, parallel tool calls were preflighted sequentially, each allowed call was stored as a deferred function, and the stored entries were later invoked with Promise.all. The deferred function unconditionally called the prepared tool and the post-execution finalizer without rechecking the shared abort signal. If a later preflight aborted the run, a call that had already been prepared but had not yet been invoked could still perform its side effect and invoke the post-execution result hook. The immediate aborted-preparation branch instead emitted an error outcome directly, so entries in one batch could follow inconsistent cancellation paths.
after: The pinned commit adds an abort check at deferred-entry invocation in the parallel executor. When the shared signal is already aborted, the entry skips tool execution and post-execution finalization, synthesizes an error outcome with the text "Operation aborted", emits tool_execution_end for that call, and returns it to the existing ordered result path. The common path then persists a toolResult message for every recorded call. title: feat(browser-use): support concurrent sessions sharing a Chrome profile
before: At parent commit 91a868d9c183e46771993aff89c7f7bbfd509b25, the checkout contains no packages/browser-use tree and no pinned Browser Use SDK, Chrome bridge, Playwright session, or related tests. The requested concurrent-session capability therefore has no implementation state in this parent under the scoped package.
after: At pinned commit 1c193a9a3e3e09db6cd44ab60b4515f2220a6175, a new Playwright-based Browser Use SDK and local Chrome bridge exist. The implemented contract is explicitly single-session per OS user: one session may control multiple tabs, a second session fails with BROWSER_USE_BUSY, and future concurrent sessions are documented as follow-up work requiring isolated ownership, event routing, cleanup, and reconnect behavior. Thus the pinned after-state does not establish support for concurrent Browser Use sessions sharing one Chrome profile.
diff: The pinned commit adds the Browser Use package, bilingual architecture documentation, a framed local Chrome-extension transport with per-user socket ownership and stale-socket recovery, Playwright CDP target/session routing, per-tab attachment serialization, runtime start/stop and stale-session invalidation, SDK proxies, and extensive unit tests. These changes coordinate one Browser Use runtime across multiple tabs and overlapping attach/cleanup operations, and reject a second runtime that attempts to bind the live bridge socket. They do not implement the target issue's multi-session isolation contract; the design explicitly places concurrent-session ownership/event-routing/cleanup/reconnect isolation in future work. Because the issue body, discussion, timeline, and linked PR are unavailable and the pinned commit identifies a different feature (#11241), this is retained as a non-promotable bounded episode with no target Change Actions or Issue Workflow.

title: [Bug]: Multiplex: API-server turns for different profiles share one Docker sandbox when their opening messages match
before: Before b5f587dba8b1852127c6cc3d7e3d98dceedbf94d, the parent implementation used the alias-resolved raw task/session id directly for a session-isolated backend. A multiplexed process serving multiple profiles could therefore put identical header-less API-server fingerprints into the same _active_environments slot: the second profile could attach to the first profile's sandbox, including its image, mounts, and exported environment. The separate session-cwd map also indexed record, read, and clear operations by the raw id, so one profile could overwrite, read, or clear another profile's working-directory state. There was no shared profile/home qualifier for these raw-id paths, although ordinary no-override behavior was intentionally raw-keyed.
after: After the change, a context-local routed home/profile scope is converted into a stable qualifier: named profiles use a profile-qualified prefix, the canonical default uses profile:default, and otherwise the active home realpath is used, with an error-safe textual fallback. Session-isolated task ids are alias-resolved and then qualified before they index the active environment cache; with no routed override they remain raw. The session-cwd record, get, and clear operations apply the same qualification symmetrically, so identical raw ids in different routed profiles use independent cwd slots. Existing persistent-Docker profile-key branches and ordinary single-profile/no-override raw-key behavior remain unchanged.
diff: The parent-to-commit diff changes exactly two files. In tools/terminal_tool.py it adds the routed home qualifier and generic task-key qualification helper, applies qualification to the session-isolated container-key branch, and changes the session-cwd record/get/clear trio to use the same helper; the terminal call-site comment documents that the centralized functions keep worker-thread callers symmetric. In tests/tools/test_docker_session_isolation.py it adds the TestRoutedScopeQualification regression class with six tests covering legacy no-override behavior, named-profile qualification, identical fingerprint collisions across named and default profiles, subagent alias qualification, symmetric cwd isolation/clear behavior, and raw cwd storage without an override. The implementation portion is 61 insertions and 7 deletions; the test addition is 98 lines.
